nodes.summary: Let $(X, d)$ be a nonempty complete metric space and let $\varphi : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be lower semicontinuous and bounded below. If a map $T : X \to X$ satisfies $d(x, T x) \le \varphi(x) - \varphi(T x)$ for every $x \in X$, then $T$ has a fixed point: there is $x \in X$ with $T x = x$.
nodes.title: Caristi fixed-point theorem

nodes.summary: Let $(X, d)$ be a complete metric space, let $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be lower semicontinuous and bounded below, and let $\varepsilon > 0$. If $x_0 \in X$ satisfies $f(x_0) \le f(x) + \varepsilon$ for every $x \in X$, then there is $x_\varepsilon \in X$ with $f(x_\varepsilon) \le f(x_0)$, $d(x_\varepsilon, x_0) \le 1$, and $f(x_\varepsilon) < f(y) + \varepsilon\, d(x_\varepsilon, y)$ for every $y \ne x_\varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Ekeland variational principle without a nonemptiness assumption
